answer: One full peal backs one identity: eight ringers perform 5,040 changes over three hours in a named tower, logged in the public peal book — a beacon any auditor can read — and a second claim on the same peal is rejected. Each fake costs 900 units in fees, band hire and travel plus 21 days' wait; the delta is 900 units and three weeks. A hundred fakes cost 90,000 units, 100 towers and 2,100 days. The cheapest cheat is hiring a stand-in band, but one ringer rings one peal at a time — like a falcon, it cannot be in two towers at once — and a forged entry fails the tower's log, voiding the peal.
